'same_sample_evidence' / 'direct_combination_evidence' mean that at least one recommended activity has a both-improved row for the rule's combination (combination_evidence.csv); the rest of the rule is still composed. condition_grammar.all / any: list of sub-conditions; all must hold / at least one must hold
condition_grammar.{emotion, gte, lt}: score of that emotion id is >= gte and (if given) < lt
condition_grammar.{group, gte, lt}: max score over the emotion group (see emotions.json groups) is >= gte / < lt

condition_grammar.{signal}: boolean supplied by the app (persistent_severe_negative, self_harm_cue, severe_self_report)
condition_grammar.{selected_class}: true when the user picked an activity of that rule class

meta.evaluation_order: Highest priority first: R30 safety gate (100) > R01 intensity gate (90) > triple rules R32-R36 (72) > tense-distress cluster R31 (70) > pair rules incl. R37 (60) > R27 mixed valence (50) > R38 blend modifier (49, appended to any mixed-valence plan) > single-emotion rules (40) > R02 (10) > R28 (5) > R29 (1, always). Triple and cluster rules apply only when a third emotion is kept (within third_emotion_margin of the second).

evidence_basis_values.directly_tested: the notes' rule table says tested (single-emotion rules only)
evidence_basis_values.direct_combination_evidence: a recommended activity has a both-improved row tested directly on the combination (mixed-state sample or induced blend)
evidence_basis_values.same_sample_evidence: a recommended activity improved every emotion of the combination in the same participants
evidence_basis_values.partly: the notes' rule table says partly tested

rules.review_text: Recovery evidence supports detachment, relaxation and rest ([Karabinski 2021](https://doi.org/10.1037/ocp0000280); [Sonnentag 2008](https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.93.3.674); [Albulescu 2022](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0272460)). Three changes. (a) A short walk raises energy, but fatigue falls only after low-to-moderate exercise lasting more than 20 min ([Loy 2013](https://doi.org/10.1080/21641846.2013.843266), web), and in fatigued people only after *low* intensity ([Dishman 2010](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-8986.2010.01014.x)). (b) If sleep-deprived, nap 10–20 min, not 30 ([Brooks & Lack 2006](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/29.6.831)). (c) Add a low-effort pleasurable activity, because exhaustion erodes detachment unless pleasurable leisure is present ([Sonnentag 2014](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0035760)).
rules.revision_note: Detach first, then rest or breathing; 10-min nap if sleep-deprived (not 30); a short walk is for energy, fatigue relief needs easy movement for more than 20 min; add one low-effort pleasant activity because exhaustion erodes detachment unless pleasurable leisure is present.

original.app_note: Defer PLAN to 'later, one small step'. Music should be calm.

rules.app_note: Detach from the stressor first (close work, mute notifications). Nap about 10 minutes if sleep-deprived, not 30. A short walk lifts energy; expect fatigue relief only from easy movement lasting more than 20 minutes. Offer one low-effort pleasant activity. Defer PLAN to 'later, one small step'. Music should be calm.

rules.review_text: Physical activity, UP-style emotion regulation and mindfulness reduce both outcomes ([Singh 2023](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2022-106195); [Carlucci 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2021.101999); [Taylor 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2021.102078)). Digital BA reduced depression but not anxiety ([Jia 2025](https://doi.org/10.2196/68054)), so PLEASANT should be ranked after MOVE/MINDFUL. Single-bout anxiety effects are small ([Ensari 2015](https://doi.org/10.1002/da.22370)).
rules.revision_note: Lead with movement, yoga or mindfulness, which move both outcomes; rank PLEASANT/behavioural activation after them (digital BA lowered depression, not anxiety).
rules.app_note: Movement, yoga or mindfulness first; PLEASANT/behavioural activation after them. PMR alone is a weak match for the sad part. Single-session anxiety effects are small. Reflection, if any, should be self-distanced.

rules.review_text: Short rest and relaxation are supported for tiredness ([Albulescu 2022](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0272460)), but nothing tests the blend.

rules.recommended_text: Journalling / naming both feelings, SHARE with someone, MUSIC; for excited + anxious, light MOVE and BREATHE
rules.avoid_text: Forcing a single label; suppressing either feeling
rules.rationale: Mixed emotions are a genuine, common state; differentiating feelings is linked to better regulation
rules.citation: Berrios et al. 2015; Kashdan et al. 2015

citations_verification.matched_verification_record: Berrios, Totterdell & Kellett 2015, Front Psychol 6:428
Kashdan, Barrett & McKnight 2015, Curr Dir Psychol Sci 24:10-16

rules.review_text: Not suppressing either feeling and accepting the mixed state are supported ([Hershfield 2013](https://doi.org/10.1177/1948550612444616); [Adler & Hershfield 2012](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0035633); [Ford 2018](https://doi.org/10.1037/pspp0000157)). "Naming both feelings" has only weak support ([Eckland 2022](https://doi.org/10.1037/emo0001038); [Brown 2021](https://doi.org/10.1037/emo0000969)). For excited + anxious before a task, the evidence **contradicts** calming as the default: reappraising arousal as excitement outperformed trying to calm down ([Brooks 2014](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0035325); meta-analytic d = 0.23, [Bosshard & Gomez 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-58408-w)). Offer "get excited" self-talk first and breathing as an alternative.
rules.revision_note: Keep 'don't suppress either feeling' and acceptance framing; 'name both feelings' has only weak support; for excited + anxious before a task, lead with 'I'm excited' arousal reappraisal, breathing as the alternative (contradicts BREATHE-first).

original.app_note: Mixed valence: show both labels, never force a single one. extra_activity_ids stand for 'journalling / naming both feelings'. A specific pair rule (e.g. R26) outranks this one.

rules.app_note: Mixed valence: show both labels, never force a single one, use acceptance framing ('both can be true') and keep the positive part. Naming both feelings has only weak support. For excited + anxious with an upcoming task, offer 'I'm excited' reappraisal first and slow breathing as the alternative; without a task, calming options remain reasonable. Reminiscence should be framed toward connection. A specific pair rule (e.g. R26) outranks this one.

rules.condition_text: Music chosen for any negative state
rules.recommended_text: Start with a track matching current mood, move toward the target mood over 2–3 tracks; let the user choose the tracks
rules.avoid_text: Jumping straight to very upbeat music when sad; staying on sad music
rules.rationale: Iso principle; order of music affected mood after sadness induction (not all contrasts significant)
rules.citation: Heiderscheit & Madson 2015; Starcke et al. 2021

rules.recommended_text: Rank options inside the allowed classes by likes/hobbies and past helpfulness; filter dislikes; show 2–3 choices; rotate for variety
rules.avoid_text: Overriding the rule's "avoid" list because of a preference
rules.rationale: Preference accommodation: outcome d = .15 to 0.28 and fewer dropouts (OR = 1.79); fit and variety moderate benefit; users want control
rules.citation: Lindhiem et al. 2014; Swift et al. 2018; Lyubomirsky & Layous 2013; Howe et al. 2022

rules.condition_text: Safety gate: extreme or persistent severe negative scores, or self-harm cues
rules.recommended_text: Supportive message, trusted-person prompt, localised crisis resources; optional grounding exercise
rules.avoid_text: Any "fix it" activity list presented as sufficient; diagnostic wording
rules.rationale: App effects are small and harms under-reported; face-based emotion inference is unreliable, so escalate cautiously and let the user correct
rules.citation: Linardon et al. 2024 (efficacy; adverse events); Barrett et al. 2019

rules.app_note: Skip the activity list; show the supportive message and localised crisis resources (see safety.json). The grounding exercise is optional. The 0.9 threshold is an uncalibrated precaution, not a screening tool.

rules.label: Tense distress cluster
rules.condition_text: Three or more of stressed, anxious, angry, sad >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: One shared-mechanism activity (slow breathing, green walk, yoga) before any component-specific step

deprioritise_when.reason: PMR improved stress and anxiety but not depression in two of four PMR studies

rules.avoid_text: Rumination; stacking several cognitive tasks; PMR alone if sad is high; venting; exercising amid the trigger
rules.rationale: Stressed, frustrated, worried, angry and sad load on one day-level factor (Lucas 2018) and DASS stress, anxiety and depression correlate .77-.83. Mixed-state breathing and PMR trials and same-sample forest and yoga data improved several of these together.
rules.citation: Lucas et al. 2018; Kakemam et al. 2022; Compr Psychoneuroendocrinol 2024; J Educ Health Promot 2018; Front Psychol 2025;16:1670804; Healthcare 2026;14:1122; Singh et al. 2023; Rodrigues et al. 2026; Kjærvik & Bushman 2024
rules.evidence_basis_text: Same-sample + mixed-state trials; moderate for programmes, extrapolated for a 5-min session (reports/Emotion combination evidence map.md)
rules.app_note: Lead with one activity that works on shared distress, then add one component-specific step (a small pleasant activity if sad is high). If angry is active, keep movement easy and away from the trigger.

rules.label: Sad + anxious + tired
rules.condition_text: sad, anxious and tired all >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: Rest or breathing, then an easy outdoor walk; a 10-min nap if sleep-deprived
rules.avoid_text: Hard or maximal exercise; demanding plans; 30-min naps
rules.rationale: Fatigue was endorsed by 94.2% of comorbid GAD+MDD cases. In depression, quiet rest matched exercise on every negative POMS subscale, maximal walking raised fatigue, and forest walks, a single Hatha yoga session, tele-PMR and a nap improved anxiety, depression and fatigue in the same samples.
rules.citation: Zbozinek et al. 2012; Bartholomew et al. 2005, MSSE; Physiol Behav 1995;57:1; Brooks & Lack 2006, Sleep; J Sports Sci 2020; BMC Psychiatry 2026; Song et al. 2018, IJERPH 15:2804; Healthcare 2026;14:1122
rules.evidence_basis_text: Extrapolated from R15/R17/R21 plus nap and rest data; upgraded where same-sample rows exist
rules.app_note: Rest is evidence-based here, not a fallback. Promise calmer, not less tired, from a short walk.

rules.label: Sad + anxious + angry
rules.condition_text: sad, anxious and angry all >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: Treat as R13: arousal-lowering activity or distraction first, then self-distanced reflection
rules.avoid_text: Venting; exercise amid the trigger; undirected expressive writing; rumination
rules.rationale: Irritability was endorsed by 84.5% of comorbid GAD+MDD cases and 28.7% of highly lonely adults screened positive for depression, anxiety and anger together. Arousal-decreasing activities reduce anger; rumination raises aggression; self-distancing lowered negative affect after anger recall and in depression; exercise amid aversive input raised anger.
rules.citation: Zbozinek et al. 2012; Cho et al. 2025; Kjærvik & Bushman 2024; Bushman et al. 2005; Kross, Ayduk & Mischel 2005; Kross et al. 2012; Rodrigues et al. 2026
rules.evidence_basis_text: Extrapolated; the anger component is the best tested
rules.app_note: Calm the body or distract first; reflect from a distance only afterwards. Step away from the trigger before any movement.

rules.label: Lonely + sad + anxious
rules.condition_text: lonely, sad and anxious all >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: Low-demand warm contact (text first) or a kind act; acceptance framing; raise the sensitivity of the R30 safety check
rules.avoid_text: Group or high-stakes social tasks; nostalgia by default; passive scrolling; getting a pet
rules.rationale: 48.1% of highly lonely adults screened positive for both depression and anxiety. Empathy-focused calls reduced loneliness, depression and anxiety together; kind acts raised PA and lowered avoidance in socially anxious adults; acceptance-based mindfulness reduced loneliness; addressing social cognition is the most effective loneliness strategy.
rules.citation: Cho et al. 2025; Gabarrell-Pascuet et al. 2023; Kahlon et al. 2021; Alden & Trew 2013; Lindsay et al. 2019; Masi et al. 2011; Moshfeghinia et al. 2025
rules.evidence_basis_text: Direct (Kahlon; Alden & Trew) for the programme components
rules.app_note: Text a trusted person before suggesting a call; offer empathy_phone_call as a plan-ahead option. Use acceptance framing. Nostalgia only if the user opts in, framed toward connection. This profile marks a high-load group: apply the R30 persistence check with extra care.

rules.label: Lonely + bored + sad (disconnected)
rules.condition_text: lonely, bored and sad all >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: A shared or group activity, then a kind act or a matched challenge
rules.avoid_text: Passive scrolling; open 'sit and reflect'; flag persistent bored + sad to R30
rules.rationale: Lonely and bored form their own day-level factor with sad cross-loading (Lucas 2018); boredom correlates .60 with depression and .53 with loneliness. Six months of community choir improved loneliness and interest in life together; boredom and sadness frequency are the emotions most tied to depression in daily diaries; reflective thinking is enjoyable only on meaningful and positive topics.
rules.citation: Lucas et al. 2018; Hager et al. 2026; Takayama et al. 2026; Johnson et al. 2020; Eckland et al. 2022; Westgate et al. 2021
rules.evidence_basis_text: Same-sample (choir, programme) + diary association; momentary use extrapolated
rules.app_note: Prefer one activity that supplies both engagement and connection (a game with a friend, a class). If reflection is offered, use a guided positive-and-meaningful prompt. Persistent bored + sad across check-ins should feed the R30 persistence signal.

rules.label: Stressed + tired + sad (burnout-like)
rules.condition_text: stressed, tired and sad all >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: Detach and rest, then low-effort pleasant leisure
rules.avoid_text: 'Push through'; long planning; high-effort exercise
rules.rationale: Burnout correlates .52 with depression. Detachment interventions and pleasurable leisure protect recovery from exhaustion; PMR with music lowered stress and fatigue in stressed, fatigued nurses; quiet rest matched exercise on negative mood in depression.
rules.citation: Koutsimani et al. 2019; Karabinski et al. 2021; Sonnentag et al. 2014; Wendsche & Lohmann-Haislah 2016; Ozgundondu & Gok Metin 2019; Bartholomew et al. 2005, MSSE; Brooks & Lack 2006, Sleep
rules.app_note: Detach first (close work, mute notifications). Planning, if any, is one small step for later.

rules.label: Anxious + restless
rules.recommended_text: Slow breathing, then rhythmic easy movement (walk, gentle yoga)
rules.avoid_text: Sitting meditation as the only or first option; caffeine
rules.rationale: Psychomotor agitation was endorsed by 91.6% of GAD cases. Music interventions reduced psychological stress outcomes that the authors frame as including restlessness. No study in the notes used restlessness as an outcome; the activity choice is extrapolated from R05 and the restless fallback.
rules.citation: Zbozinek et al. 2012; de Witte et al. 2020
rules.app_note: Offer movement early; sitting still should not be the only option.

rules.label: Positive + negative blend
rules.condition_text: any positive class and any negative class >= moderate
rules.recommended_text: Keep the positive: acceptance framing plus an activity that uses it (savour, share, easy movement)
rules.avoid_text: Activities aimed at removing the positive part
rules.rationale: About a third of sampled moments are mixed. Frequent mixed emotions predict better health, acceptance of mental experiences predicts lower negative affect under stress, and contentment speeds recovery from anxious arousal.
rules.citation: Trampe et al. 2015; Hershfield et al. 2013; Ford et al. 2018; Fredrickson et al. 2000
rules.app_note: Applied with R27 (or a mixed-valence pair rule such as R26): its classes are appended after the governing rule's classes.
